issues.title: 2020 XT6 Start/Stop Accumulator May Be Missing Endcap Bolts — Recall 20V668000
issues.description: Only the 2020 model year of the Cadillac XT6 falls inside this GM recall, which addresses a start/stop transmission accumulator that may have left the plant with bolts missing from its endcap. Because those bolts hold the endcap against transmission oil pressure, the missing hardware can allow a transmission oil leak. NHTSA's consequence statement is blunt about where that goes: the leak may progress to a loss of propulsion, increasing crash risk, and transmission fluid in the presence of an ignition source may increase the risk of fire. The same defect was found across a range of 2018-2020 Chevrolet, Buick, GMC and Cadillac vehicles; the XT6's exposure is the 2020 year alone.
issues.solution: Free of charge at a Cadillac dealer: the technician inspects the start/stop transmission accumulator on your 2020 XT6 and replaces the unit if any endcap bolts are missing. The recall opened to owners on December 15, 2020. If you bought the XT6 used, do not assume the previous owner had it done — check the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, then book the inspection through Cadillac customer service at 1-800-458-8006. GM's recall number is N202313440.
symptoms: Transmission oil leak
Vehicle loses propulsion

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 20V668000 — 2020 Cadillac XT6 Start/Stop Accumulator Endcap Missing Bolts

issues.title: 3.6L LGX Engine Oil Migrating Into the Cooling System Through Block Porosity — Overheating with Sludge in the Radiator
issues.description: GM bulletin 21-NA-108 (which superseded PIP5257E) covers engine overheating with the cooling system contaminated by engine oil, and it lists the 2020-2021 Cadillac XT6 with the 3.6L LGX V6 among the affected applications. The failure is not a head gasket in the usual sense: pressurized oil from the main oil gallery migrates into a coolant water jacket through porosity or a thin-wall casting defect in the engine block. Because oil pressure is far higher than coolant pressure, oil pushes into the coolant rather than the other way round, and the surge tank and radiator fill with a thick brown oil-and-coolant emulsion that looks like a milkshake. That emulsion will not carry heat, so the engine overheats, and it plugs the radiator and heater core. GM bulletins 21-NA-147 and 22-NA-240 cover the related diagnosis of a coolant and/or oil leak with the malfunction indicator lamp on. This is engine-code specific — it is an LGX 3.6L casting issue and is not a claim about the 2.0L LSY turbo four also sold in the XT6.
issues.solution: Do not just flush the coolant and refill — the contamination will come straight back. Follow the bulletin's diagnostic sequence, which confirms the source by pressure-testing and by checking whether the oil level drops while the coolant turns to emulsion. Where the leak path is traced to block porosity, the repair is an engine block or complete engine replacement, which is why this is worth pursuing under the 6-year/70,000-mile GM powertrain warranty while it is still in force; document the concern in writing at the first sign of contamination. If contamination is confirmed, the radiator, surge tank, heater core and oil cooler all need flushing or replacement, since emulsified oil coats every passage. Out of warranty an engine replacement on an XT6 typically runs $8,000-$12,000.
symptoms: Engine temperature climbing or overheat warning
Thick brown or tan milkshake-like sludge in the coolant surge tank and radiator
Engine oil level dropping with no external leak and no visible smoke
Coolant loss
Malfunction indicator lamp illuminated
Weak or oily-smelling cabin heat as the heater core plugs

issues.title: Low-Speed TCC Shudder Must Be Confirmed Before a Fluid Drain and Fill
issues.description: GM PIP5608F covers 2020-2021 XT6 vehicles with 9-speed transmissions RPO M3G or M3W when torque-converter clutch shudder occurs on re-apply after a shift at 40 mph or below. GM identifies possible excessive assembly lubricant in the fluid and requires confirmation with TCC slip data or the scan-tool command test.
issues.solution: Have a qualified transmission technician verify RPO M3G or M3W and confirm the event is TCC shudder using slip-speed data or the commanded-on test. If the bulletin criteria are met, follow the GM DEXRON VI drain-and-fill procedure and drive at least 200 miles before judging the repair. Do not use a universal additive or flush kit. The exact ShowMeTheParts lookup returned no transmission-fluid candidate.
symptoms: Low-speed shudder on TCC re-apply after a shift
Concern occurs at 40 mph or below
Concern changes when TCC is commanded on

citations.title: GM Preliminary Information PIP5608F - 2020-2021 XT6 Low-Speed TCC Shudder

issues.title: Auto Start-Stop Harshness and Battery Issues
issues.description: The auto start-stop system engages and disengages harshly, causing the vehicle to shudder on restart. The AGM battery required for the system degrades quickly, and when it weakens, the start-stop system becomes erratic or disables itself. Many owners find the system intrusive.
issues.solution: Replace the AGM battery with a fresh ACDelco unit if the system is not functioning properly. Have the battery monitor sensor reset after replacement. GM has released recalibrations to improve start-stop smoothness. Aftermarket start-stop eliminator modules are available for owners who want to permanently disable the feature.
symptoms: Harsh restart vibration
Start-stop not functioning
Battery warning message
Multiple systems acting erratic
Slow cranking on restart

issues.title: Electric Power Steering Rack Failure — "Steering Assist Is Reduced / Service Power Steering" with C0460 or C0545
issues.description: XT6 owners report a "Steering Assist is Reduced — Drive with Care" or "Service Power Steering" message in the driver information center, usually with a noticeable increase in steering effort. GM bulletin 20-NA-215 covers this condition on the XT5 and XT6 and ties it to DTCs C0460 and/or C0545 stored in the power steering module. The XT6 uses a belt-drive electric rack with the motor and control module integrated into the steering gear, so an internal fault or a torque-sensor signal fault sets the code and the module deliberately cuts or reduces assist rather than allowing erratic assist. Steering is still mechanically connected — the car remains steerable — but effort rises sharply, which is most alarming at parking-lot speeds or in an evasive maneuver. Owners also describe a separate, milder version where assist fades after sustained low-speed maneuvering and returns once the system cools; that thermal derate is normal protection, not a failed rack, and it clears itself.
issues.solution: Have the power steering module scanned first. A stored C0460 or C0545 per bulletin 20-NA-215 calls for replacement of the complete steering gear assembly — the module is not serviced separately. After the rack is replaced the steering angle sensor must be recalibrated with a capable scan tool or the system will not function and the message will return. Out of warranty a rack and calibration typically runs roughly $1,500-$2,600 at a dealer. Before replacing anything, rule out the thermal derate (assist returns after cooling, no stored code) and a weak battery or poor ground, either of which can trigger a false assist-reduced message on this platform. The XT6's powertrain warranty does not cover this, but the 4-year/50,000-mile bumper-to-bumper coverage does.
symptoms: "Steering Assist is Reduced — Drive with Care" message in the DIC
"Service Power Steering" warning
Steering suddenly becomes very heavy, especially at parking speeds
Assist cuts out intermittently and returns after a restart
Sometimes accompanied by other electrical warnings on the same drive

issues.title: Loss of Cabin Heat Caused by an Engine Control Module Software Anomaly — Bulletin 22-NA-094
issues.description: GM bulletin 22-NA-094, issued July 2022, addresses a loss of cabin heat on the Cadillac XT6 and XT5. Owners get little or no warm air from the vents even after the engine reaches operating temperature — the complaint typically shows up in cold weather and is easy to misdiagnose as a stuck thermostat, an air pocket in the cooling system, a blend door actuator, or a plugged heater core. GM traced it instead to a software anomaly in the engine control module: the ECM's thermal management strategy does not bring coolant temperature up or route flow to the heater core as intended, so the heater has nothing hot to work with. Because the fault is calibration rather than hardware, no part is actually broken, and owners who let a shop chase it mechanically can spend hundreds of dollars replacing a perfectly good thermostat or heater core before the real fix is applied.
issues.solution: The fix is a reprogram, not a part. Per bulletin 22-NA-094, the correction is to reprogram the engine control module with the updated calibration; this is a dealer or capable-shop operation using GM's programming tools and takes about an hour. Ask specifically for bulletin 22-NA-094 by number. Before authorizing a thermostat or heater core replacement for a no-heat complaint on an XT6, confirm the ECM calibration is current — under the 4-year/50,000-mile bumper-to-bumper warranty the reprogram is free, and even out of warranty it typically runs $100-$200 against $600-$1,400 for a heater core job that would not have fixed it.
symptoms: Little or no heat from the vents in cold weather
Cabin takes an unusually long time to warm up, or never does
Engine coolant temperature gauge reads normal while the vents blow cool
Heat is intermittent — works on some drives and not others

citations.title: GM Service Bulletin 22-NA-094 — Loss of Cabin Heat (ECM reprogram)

issues.title: AWD Power Transfer Unit Fluid Leak
issues.description: The Power Transfer Unit (PTU) on AWD-equipped XT6 models develops seal leaks that allow fluid to seep out. Low PTU fluid causes the internal gears and bearings to wear prematurely, eventually producing a whining noise. The PTU is not included in routine maintenance schedules, so leaks often go unnoticed.
issues.solution: Inspect the PTU seals and replace if leaking. Top off with the GM-specified PTU fluid. If the PTU is already noisy from running low on fluid, replacement is required as the unit is not rebuildable. Add PTU fluid level check to your routine maintenance schedule every 15,000 miles.
symptoms: Fluid leak near front of transmission
Whining noise from front drivetrain
AWD malfunction warning
Oil spots on driveway

issues.title: Rearview Camera Cuts Out Due to Bad Coaxial Cable Crimp on Surround Vision-Equipped XT6 (Recall 22V709000)
issues.description: If your 2020 or 2021 Cadillac XT6 was ordered with the optional Surround Vision feature, it may be part of NHTSA recall 22V709000. GM found that the coaxial cable connectors carrying the rearview camera signal may have been crimped improperly, and a faulty crimp can cause the rearview camera to fail outright or work only intermittently. The practical effect for an XT6 driver is a missing or unreliable rear image when reversing, which NHTSA notes reduces rear visibility and increases crash risk. XT6s without Surround Vision are not covered. The campaign as a whole spans 95,231 vehicles across all the models it includes - that number is for the entire campaign and says nothing about how many XT6s are involved. GM tracks the recall internally as N222378380 and mailed owner letters on January 18, 2023.
issues.solution: Dealers replace the affected coaxial cables at no charge to the owner. Take the XT6 to any Cadillac dealer and ask them to perform recall N222378380 / NHTSA 22V709000. Before you go, run your VIN through nhtsa.gov/recalls - it will tell you whether your XT6 is genuinely affected and whether the cable replacement has already been done. Cadillac customer service is at 1-800-458-8006 if the dealer cannot help.
symptoms: No rearview camera image when backing up
Camera view flickers or works only intermittently
Surround Vision rear view unavailable

citations.title: NHTSA Recall 22V709000 - 2020-2021 Cadillac XT6 Rearview Camera Coaxial Cable (GM N222378380)

issues.title: 3.6L V6 Timing Chain Concern (XT6)
issues.description: The XT6 uses the GM 3.6L V6 (LGX) which has a documented history of timing chain stretch across the GM lineup. While the LGX generation is improved over earlier 3.6L variants, the three-chain design with plastic guides remains a long-term reliability concern. Most XT6s are still too new for widespread timing chain failures, but owners should monitor for early signs and plan for preventive replacement around 100,000-120,000 miles based on the engine's history in other models.
issues.solution: Monitor for timing chain rattle on cold starts. If codes or rattle develop, complete timing chain replacement is needed. Preventive replacement at 100,000-120,000 miles is wise based on the 3.6L's track record. Same Cloyes 9-0753S kit as other 3.6L applications.
symptoms: Rattling on cold start that goes away when warm
Check engine light with timing correlation codes at higher mileage
Rough idle developing gradually

issues.title: 9-Speed Automatic Transmission Shudder and Harsh Shifts
issues.description: The XT6's GM 9T65 9-speed automatic transmission exhibits shuddering during light throttle acceleration between 25-50 mph, similar to driving over rumble strips. The torque converter clutch wears prematurely, contaminating the transmission fluid.
issues.solution: A transmission fluid flush with the updated Mobil 1 Blue Label fluid resolves mild cases. Severe cases require torque converter replacement. A GM TSB authorizes fluid flush as the first repair attempt.
symptoms: Shuddering at 25-50 mph
Vibration during light acceleration
Harsh 1-2 shift
Transmission hesitation
Feels like driving over rumble strips
Shudder worse when transmission is warm

issues.title: Water Leaks Into the Interior Through Pinholes in the Roof Panel Laser Braze — Wet Carpet and Inoperative Liftgate Actuator
issues.description: GM bulletin 19-NA-167 covers water leaking into the interior on the 2020-2021 Cadillac XT6 (alongside the 2017-2021 XT5 and GMC Acadia). Owners find wet carpet or headliner at the front and/or rear, on either side, typically after rain or a car wash. The cause is not the sunroof drains that owners and shops usually chase first: it is pinhole voids in the laser braze joint between the roof panel and the outer body ring, and in the seam sealer over it. The bulletin says the pinholes are most often found near the top of the windshield at the A-pillars, or near the top of the liftgate at the D-pillars. Water entering at the D-pillars runs down into the rear of the vehicle, and the bulletin specifically notes that on the XT6 the liftgate actuator may become noisy or inoperative as a result — so an electrical complaint at the tailgate is a symptom of the body leak, not a separate failure. Left alone, trapped water rots carpet padding, grows mold, and corrodes rear body connectors.
issues.solution: Have the shop follow 19-NA-167 rather than starting with sunroof drain cleaning. The diagnosis is a water test of the roof-to-body laser braze at the A-pillar and D-pillar corners to find the pinholes, followed by resealing the braze joint and seam sealer at the void. Any water-damaged carpet and padding must be lifted and fully dried, and a liftgate actuator that has been soaked usually needs replacement even after the leak is sealed. Expect roughly $300-$1,200 for the leak repair and drying at a dealer, more if the actuator or a wet module has to be replaced; this is a factory body-sealing defect, so ask about warranty coverage before authorizing a paid repair.
symptoms: Wet carpet or floor mats, front and/or rear
Damp headliner or water dripping from the A-pillar or D-pillar trim
Musty or mildew smell in the cabin
Power liftgate actuator noisy, slow, or inoperative
Water appears after rain or a car wash
